newsitem.title: USA: Boeing says MD jets have brighter future.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says MD jets have brighter future.

text.p: Boeing Co. President and chief operating officer Harry Stonecipher said the acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp. gives the former company's jets a better opportunity for sales.

In response to a question at a Washington news conference, Stonecipher said the future of the MD-80/90, MD-95 and MD-11 jets, which have won few orders in recent years, depends on companies buying them.
The news conference was monitored by telephone.
"I happen to be of the opinion that now that we are one company and have the strength of Boeing, that those products will sell better," Stonecipher said.
He pointed in particular to the new twin-jet MD-95, which has not won any orders since the product was launched in 1995 with a sale of 50 planes to ValuJet Inc.

"One of the questions was always, 'Is Douglas going to be around? Are you committed to the business?" Stonecipher said. "I think clearly people don't have to ask that question anymore, and when you have those products in a Boeing salesman's bag -- the new Boeing -- it has a better opportunity."
